Is\[\sum \frac{p_n}{2^n}\]irrational? (Here $p_n$ is the $n$th prime.)
#251: [Er58b][ErGr80,p.62][Er88c,p.103]
number theory | 
irrationality
Erdős [Er58b] proved that $\sum \frac{p_n^k}{n!}$ is irrational for every $k\geq 1$.
In [Er88c] he further conjectures that $\sum \frac{p_n^k}{2^n}$ is irrational for every $k$, and that if $g_n\geq 2$ and $g_n=o(p_n)$ then\[\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{p_n}{g_1\cdots g_n}\]is irrational. (The example $g_n=p_n+1$ shows that some condition on the growth of the $g_n$ is necessary here.)
The decimal expansion of this sum is A098990 on the OEIS.

 By summation by parts, this is equivalent to the irrationality of $\sum_n \frac{p_{n+1}-p_n}{2^n}$. It is possible that a sufficiently quantitative and uniform version of the prime tuples conjecture can resolve this problem, if it gives sufficient statistical control on the binary expansion of about $\log \log n$ consecutive prime gaps $p_{n+1}-p_n$ (which is usually of size $\asymp \log n$) to show that the binary expansion of $\sum_n \frac{p_{n+1}-p_n}{2^n}$ cannot be periodic. The theory of Shannon entropy may be helpful in this regard.

 Congrats, Johan, beat me to it! I've been working on this problem for a while as well.
My current proof gives a normality result under a local prime-pattern hypothesis implied by Kuperberg’s Conjecture 1.3. For each fixed degree and base, the input is a one-sided, averaged bound on tuple-count errors involving only tuples of size \(O(\log\log X)\).
Writing \(g_n=p_{n+1}-p_n\), the result is that\[ \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{P_{n\bmod m}(g_n)}{b^n} \]is normal to base \(b\), for every fixed integer base \(b\ge2\), fixed period \(m\), and rational polynomials \(P_0,\ldots,P_{m-1}\), provided at least one is nonconstant. For each fixed base and period, the components corresponding to each positive power of the gaps and each index class modulo \(m\) also have jointly equidistributed orbits along the powers of \(b^m\). This gives linear independence over \(\mathbb Q\) together with \(1\).
Summation by parts then gives normality of \(\sum p_n/b^n\), so conditional irrationality in #251 follows. 
The mechanism is local pattern transfer into a sieve model, followed by averaging over the position of a single interior point to obtain phase cancellation. Moving that point changes just two adjacent gaps, reducing the cancellation step to a one-variable polynomial phase whose leading coefficient is nonzero in at least one index class. The tail is controlled using only first-moment averages of the gaps, without assuming higher gap moments.
Like you, I haven't managed to make the prime result unconditional. For testing purposes I studied some related series: I've obtained unconditional normality for the "rough number" series \(\sum r_n/b^n\), where \(r_n\) enumerates the integers \(r\) with no prime factor at most \(z(r)=r^{c/\log\log r}\), for sufficiently small base-dependent \(c\). I've also obtained irrationality and nonnormality for a class of B-free series, including squarefree numbers.
For powers of the primes, I'm still stuck even conditionally: For \(\sum p_n^2/2^n\), my current argument encounters a carry term requiring look-ahead of order \(\log X\), rather than \(\log\log X\). I'd be particularly interested in whether your rare-pattern and tail-selection method could help there. Working on that now.
I'm almost done with Lean implementation and will share the write-up soon (+ AI attribution). Excited to see where Terence or future models may take this!

 The last conjecture below the main problem statement has an (overly simple) negative answer. The idea is elementary, just make the series telescope by choosing positive integers $(c_n)$ such that\[ \frac{p_n}{g_1\cdots g_n} = \frac{c_n}{g_1\cdots g_{n-1}} - \frac{c_{n+1}}{g_1\cdots g_n}, \]i.e. $c_{n+1}=c_n g_n - p_n$. Thus, one can define $(c_n)$ recursively, by only making sure that\[ c_{n+1} \equiv -p_n \ (\text{mod} \ c_n) \]and that it is bounded from below by something that grows slowly but steadily. Afterwards one just sets\[ g_n := \frac{c_{n+1}+p_n}{c_n}. \]I got ChatGPT 5.4 Pro figure out the proof and write up the details with only minimal orchestration from my side.
It is possible that Erdős also wanted $(g_n)$ to be increasing, but then it would be weird to emphasize $g_n\geq2$ and switch the notation from $a_n$ to $g_n$ for this particular problem in [Er88c].
